title: FedEMoE: Improving Personalization on Heterogeneous Federated Learning via Elastic Mixture of Experts Architecture
claim: Decoupling personalized and shared knowledge via local expert groups plus a server that diagnoses and elastically restructures the shared expert improves heterogeneous collaboration.
layout: Clients stacked left, server panel right, numbered steps ①–⑧, bottom legend
description: A system diagram with three stacked gray client panels (Client 1, Client 2, Client K) on the left, each in a different color theme (blue, yellow, red), and a light-blue Server panel on the right. Inside each client, a multi-scale feature extractor sits at the left. Next to it are a personalized expert group (PEG) and a shared expert (SE) drawn as layered neural networks. Then come the activated experts, a device icon (computer, phone or watch), a dataset icon and a bar chart. Thick gray arrows (④) carry client updates to the server, and purple arrows (⑧) carry the updated shared expert back. The server shows sparse aggregation (⑤), restructuring, and diagnosis (⑥) from singular value distribution curves. It then expands or shrinks the experts (⑦), shown by orange and green arrows. A bottom legend explains the icons: knowledge exchange, under-fitting (fire), over-fitting (ice), expand, shrink. Circled step numbers guide the reading order.

abstract: Heterogeneous federated learning (HtFL) has emerged as a promising approach to address heterogeneity in local computational resources and data distribution. However, existing methods cause performance degradation of model personalization because personalized and generalized knowledge are either intertwined or dominated by one of them. To address this issue, we propose a novel Elastic Mixture of Experts (EMoE) architecture on HtFL, namely FedEMoE, decoupling personalization from generalization. Specially, FedEMoE employs a multi-scale feature extraction mechanism via personalized experts to enrich personalized knowledge. Furthermore, we design an elastic shared expert to break the transferred knowledge bottleneck across heterogeneous client models. The elastic shared expert can adaptively expand or shrink according to the status of each expert by the weight spectrum analysis, respectively. Extensive experiments across statistical and model heterogeneity settings demonstrate that FedEMoE significantly outperforms state-of-the art methods on the accuracy of each heterogeneous model over diverse datasets.
